The distance-time graph shows information about part of a car journey.

![q1-medium-2-19-estimating-gradients-edexcel-gcse-maths](assets/038-q1-medium-2-19-estimating-gradients-edexcel-gcse.png)

Use the graph to estimate the speed of the car at time 5 seconds.
parts.solution_md:
*In a **distance-time graph**, the **speed is equivalent to the gradient** of the graph* 
*We can estimate the speed at time 5 seconds by drawing a tangent at time 5 seconds and calculating its gradient*

> *First draw a tangent at 5 seconds. This should be a straight line (use a ruler or straight edge) touching the curve at 5 seconds, but not crossing the curve*

![E9dGc_YO_edexcel-tq-mis-2-16-m1](assets/039-e9dgc-yo-edexcel-tq-mis-2-16-m1.png)

**suitable tangent line drawn**** [1]**

> *Pick two points on the tangent, not too close to each other. Try to pick points that can be clearly read off the grid. E.g. in the diagram above, we have picked (8, 70) and (2.9, 0) *

> *Find the gradient between these two points using *$\frac{\mathrm{rise}}{\mathrm{run}}$* or *$\frac{y_{1}-y_{2}}{x_{1}-x_{2}}$* *

> *Your gradient will depend on your tangent so there is some margin of error permitted in exam questions. For the tangent drawn above, the calculation and answer would be as follows*

*gradient = *$\frac{70-0}{8-2.9}$

$\frac{rise}{run}$* ***or gradient formula used with tangent line**** [1]**

$=\frac{70}{5.1}=13.7254902...$

> *As the distance is in metres and the time is in seconds, the gradient is the speed in m/s. *

> *If your calculation does not result in an exact answer, write the answer to at least 3 significant figures*

**13.7 m/s ****[1]**** **
